extracted.intended_audience: researchers, faculty, and graduate students building academic profiles and considering post-publication peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on engaging in post-publication peer review (platform choices, benefits, and basic eligibility/procedural notes) as part of creating and managing an academic profile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value-added aspects of post-publication peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-publication peer review can add value to published papers by increasing the number of reviewers, further developing discussion about the paper, and increasing the visibility of the paper to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use post-publication review to broaden scrutiny, stimulate ongoing scholarly discussion, and raise the profile/visibility of work; these are the primary benefits highlighted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-publication review for academic profile building
rubrics_metrics.description: For academic profile building, offering post-publication peer review can highlight your in-depth subject knowledge while engaging in community building.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contributing substantive reviews publicly (or under a consistent account) may showcase expertise and help build scholarly networks; consider this when deciding to participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: PubPeer scope and participation model
rubrics_metrics.description: PubPeer allows anonymous researchers to comment on any article with a DOI, or those published as preprints in arXiv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create a PubPeer account and username to keep track of the reviews you write. Be aware that the platform permits anonymous commenting, which affects visibility and attribution of your reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: ScienceOpen transparent post-publication review process
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts submitted to ScienceOpen are published Open Access and evaluated in a fully transparent Post-Publication Peer Review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ScienceOpen's model emphasizes transparency of reviews and open access publication; consult ScienceOpen's peer review and comments guidelines for platform-specific expectations and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: ScienceOpen reviewer eligibility requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are required to have published at least five scientific manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ScienceOpen verifies reviewer publication records (in partnership with ORCID) to ensure reviewers meet this minimum publication threshold; this is a criterion for who may act as a reviewer on that platform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow platform-specific peer review guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Different platforms have their own guidelines (e.g., 'How to Review on PubMed Commons', 'ScienceOpen - Peer Review Guidelines', 'ScienceOpen - Guidelines for Comments').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before reviewing on a given platform, read and follow its specific peer review and commenting guidelines (covering tone, scope, eligibility, anonymity policies, and format). The page links to those platform resources for details.
